title: Resources loaded through GDScript `preload()` are never unloaded
body: ### Tested versions Tested on v4.0.4 and v4.6.2 stable builds. Behavior is likely the same in all other 4.x versions. ### System information Godot v4.6.2.stable (71f334935) - Freedesktop SDK 25.08 (Flatpak runtime) on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 760M Graphics (radeonsi, phoenix, LLVM 21.1.8, DRM 3.64, 6.18.13-200.fc43.x86_64) - AMD Ryzen 5 7640U w/ Radeon 760M Graphics (12 threads) - 14.92 GiB memory ### Issue description I'm not actually sure if this is actually a bug, or just undocumented behavior, so there could be room for discussion. At least through a quick search in the docs, I can't find any warning that `preload()` is unable to unload resources, and yet, [it is widely recommended as the default option in official docs pages](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agodotengine%2Fgodot-docs%20preload&type=code), and many non-official tutorials as well. Why this is a problem: due to its recommended status, many developers have the impression that `preload()` is faster and more performant than other resource loading methods, which it could be in small games that can fit entirely in RAM + VRAM, but as projects scale up and more resources are added to them, so does increase the likelihood of more resources being preloaded. This causes them to be pinned to memory for the entirety of the game's runtime, with no clear warning signs of how bad this can be. As a consequence, if a game preloads heavy scenes, such as entire levels, a long session might cause the game to slow down or even crash, due to the continuous pile-up of resources that never get cleaned up by Godot. That means using `preload()` is as dangerous as creating cyclic references between RefCounted objects, if not more because resources can contain large amounts of data. Notes: - This is not a memory leak, because the resources can still be loaded from the cache, so a specific resource won't be instantiated multiple times. - This seems to be directly caused by #77513, since preloads are held by compiled scripts. - Despite the similar name, the ResourcePreloader node is not affected by this. Its resources are held by the scene resource, same as `@export` vars. Example included in MRP. ### Steps to reproduce - Create some kind of resource or scene with a script; - Load another resource in that script, using the `preload()` macro; - Create an instance of the script, and then free the instance (and if using a scene, release references to it); - Use any method to verify that the preloaded resource is still in memory (ie. WeakRef.get_ref(), or static memory monitor). MRP contains a WeakRef-based example. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Project structure: - main.tscn - startup scene - icon.tscn - scene loaded dynamically by main.tscn, with its own dependencies - resources/* - plain Resource instances that are used by icon.tscn Use "Spawn Icon" button to add an instance of the icon and print some logs, then "Delete Icon" to delete the latest added icon instance and print more logs about its resources. Notice "script_preloaded" never becomes null through the WeakRef. Expected: - when the last icon instance is deleted, all unused resources should be freed OR - docs are updated to reflect `preload()` sticky memory behavior Logs: MRP Link: [preload-no-unload.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26681189/preload-no-unload.zip)
